title: Chelsea’s Levi Colwill included in England’s 55-man provisional World Cup squad
content:
Levi Colwill has been included in England’s provisional World Cup squad despite having just returned to the Chelsea first team after being injured for the majority of the 2025-26 campaign.

Colwill resumed playing for Chelsea again earlier this month after suffering an anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) injury in early August. He made his comeback as a substitute at home to Nottingham Forest on May 4 and his first start in the 1-1 draw at Liverpool last Saturday.

The 23-year-old showed he is already match sharp by playing the full match at Anfield and Chelsea interim head coach Calum McFarlane praised his performance afterwards.

England head coach Thomas Tuchel has added the Chelsea centre-half to his preliminary list, which can hold up to 55 players.

Tuchel can name just 26 players for the World Cup, which is being held in the U.S, Canada and Mexico and the squad is expected to be announced next Friday (May 22).

But Colwill will have more chances to get vital game time and improve his fitness before England’s opening game against Croatia on June 17.

Colwill is under consideration to start for Chelsea in the FA Cup Final against Manchester City on Saturday. Chelsea also have two league games – against Tottenham (May 19) and Sunderland (May 24) – before the end of the campaign.

England have two warm-up friendlies against New Zealand (June 6) and Costa Rica (June 10) in Orlando next month ahead of their opening World Cup match versus Croatia on June 17.

Colwill has won five England caps so far, with only one of those coming under Tuchel when he started the 3-1 friendly defeat to Senegal last June.

But a sign of how he was increasingly becoming part of Tuchel’s plans was that he had already been named in three matchday squads before that, although ended up being an unused substitute.
